Erin — thanks for the ping and context. Looping internal covers to propose a practical resolution. Quoting your ask below.

(Erin's message quoted)

Internal note / proposal: rather than a pure regional handoff, propose we split coverage by product line and partner specialization for Acme. Rationale:
- NimbleWorks' consult team is strong on implementation services (ETL, pipelines) but weaker on embedding/ML ops connectors where Redwood-verified runtime + observability adds the most value.
- Redwood-Prime (existing channel) has stronger enterprise GTM with the Acme procurement contacts and is better positioned for post-PoC expansion.

Proposed split (high level):
1) NimbleWorks: Implementation services + PoC delivery (Dec-March), consulting fees go to NimbleWorks; they get co-sell credit for initial deals.
2) Redwood-Prime: Account ownership for renewal/expansion, sales lead on commercial conversations, primary billing relationship.
3) Revenue credit: initial split 50/50 for first-year ACV tied to the PoC conversion, to be evaluated at Q2 review.

I've attached a simple matrix (Acme_SPLIT_MATRIX_v2.xlsx) that maps product lines to partner responsibilities and recommended contact owners. Can Sergio or Laura weigh in on the credit split and whether we should instead lock to a 60/40 to Redwood for enterprise ownership? If we can't reach quick alignment I'll escalate to Alliances leadership for tie-break.

Next steps I propose:
- Sergio: review commercial credit assumptions and confirm legal ask (MOU vs. SOW appendix)
- Laura: confirm if the CS/AM handover timeline (post-PoC) aligns with our renewal cadence
- Erin: confirm NimbleWorks' willingness to sign a short MOU outlining coverage and lead routing

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Alliances Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks for drafting, Soojin. Quick thoughts inline.

- Product-line split makes sense operationally but creates revenue recognition risk and complicates quota credit for our AMs. If Redwood-Prime retains account ownership then we should lock a higher revenue credit (60/40) to Redwood for year one.
- Alternatively, a region-first split (US east/west) would be easier to enforce in CRM and avoids cross-product invoicing. But that forces NimbleWorks to cede some service-driven opportunities they expect to capture.

I'm neutral on escalating but prefer we try to get NimbleWorks to sign an MOU that includes:
* explicit lead routing rules (HubSpot pipeline owner and referral tags)
* clear renewal ownership after 12 months unless a written handoff is agreed
* initial revenue split (suggest 60% Redwood / 40% NimbleWorks for ACV tied to our platform license)

If leadership will likely accept 60/40, I'm happy to sign off and get legal to stitch the MOU.

Sergio
Head of GTM Alliances
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme — proposed product-line split & revenue credit (decision + MOU draft)

All — summarizing decision to move forward and next steps. After weighing operational friction vs. partner expectations, Alliances leadership (Jonas + Sergio) have agreed to a middle path to unblock the PoC:

Decision summary:
- Coverage model: Product-line split for PoC delivery (NimbleWorks leads implementation), Redwood retains account ownership for expansion and billing.
- Revenue credit: 60% Redwood / 40% NimbleWorks on ACV attributable to platform license for year one; renewals revert to Redwood ownership unless a documented handoff is executed.
- Governance: short-form MOU to be signed by NimbleWorks and Acme specifying lead routing and handover triggers.

Attachments: attached MOU draft (MOU-draft-Acme.pdf) for legal review. I've also uploaded the final split matrix to the Drive link below.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Soojin: send the MOU to NimbleWorks and Acme (draft attached) — due Mon 12/1 EOD
- Sergio: confirm commercial language and queue legal (LL) for redlines — due Tue 12/2
- Jonas: cover executive approval for the 60/40 split in alliances review — done by Wed 12/3
- Erin / Acme: confirm acceptance or request edits to MOU — requested by Thu 12/4

If anyone thinks we should instead route to procurement for a partner reseller agreement, flag now; otherwise I'll proceed with the MOU path.

Thanks — Laura
